title: Ontological Flattening: Toy Models of the Collapse of Distinctions in a Represented World, the Instrument They Specified, and Its First Wave — with Wave 2 Pre-Registered (EA-FLAT-01 v0.3)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description:
MODEL COLLAPSE ASKED AT THE WIDEST ANGLE, AND THEN MEASURED. If the layer through which a population reads the world composes without reading, and its compositions become its sources, what collapses is not a model's distribution but the represented world — the set of distinctions a reader can still reach. Reality is defined operationally here and not metaphysically: the panel of distinctions the world carries that remain reachable through the layer. Flattening is the loss of a distinction from that set while the things distinguished still exist; collapse is flattening that compounds because the flattened composition is written back as a source. Closed is defined so that the finite-grammar objection cannot land: an ontology is closed when encounter cannot enlarge its distinction-generating apparatus or revise its typing rules.

FOUR TOYS, EACH SCOPED TO WHAT IT SHOWS. Sense collapse under a sharpening prior and mode-seeking aggregation takes a string with six effective senses to one; fan-out is documented, the voting aggregator is this notebook's hypothesis. A frozen type system yields a proposition with a proof: for a world acquiring types at rate lambda and an ontology able to represent at most K distinctly, representability is bounded by K/(N0 + lambda t) and goes to zero, with admission the only parameter that holds it. Compression writing, replicated over 200 seeds, is absorbing at zero exogenous floor — every seed reaches five or six distinctions by generation 30 and stays — and stationary at a level set by the floor for every floor tested. The admission sweep rejects linear preferential attachment, which cannot leave the diffuse regime, and locates the observed concentration in the bounded-admission family with within-set spread; superlinear attachment and hard and soft gates all overshoot to near-monopoly. B and C are two realizations of one closure condition, not one curve. […abridged for the catalogue; full description in this deposit's record]
content_type: Theoretical notebook with toy models, a built instrument and a pre-registered second wave
substrate: Composed 2026-09-15 by Lee Sharks with TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic), operator-directed, in three versions over one day. The four toys were written and run in session; C was replicated over 200 seeds and D swept across five mechanisms after a reviewer report supplied by the operator was verified line by line against the runs, and the report's corrections were adopted on its own terms where they held. The panel, its schema, its intake and its battery were built the same day; the twelve world-strata addresses were run by the operator and pasted, and each observation was coded against a named reference — coding by TACHYON with the operator, NOT blind, recorded as blind:false on every row, because the coder authored the panel. Elements a composition attributed to the archive were verified against the archive's texts before coding, and one attributed institutional affiliation was checked against DataCite's API and found to be introduced downstream. The wave-1 baseline was sealed and wave 2 pre-registered before any of it was written up.
methodology: Toys: pure stdlib, seeded, re-runnable; C over 200 seeds with interquartile bands and a stationarity check; D swept across linear PA, superlinear PA at two exponents, a hard gate, a soft logistic gate and a seed-only gate, compared by curve shape rather than fitted. Panel: one item per distinction set, each with an inventory from a named reference, dated where the date matters, and an address family; one observation per address per date, coded for distinctions reached, resolution, false distinctions, presented sources, coder and blind flag, with the transcript seated in the Capture Registry and its address id carried. Battery: N_eff^sense per item and form, R_new over dated distinctions, DS on the latest observation per form, false-distinction rate, N_eff^source, recovery and write-back. Wave 1 run on one surface, signed out, in one session. The baseline is sealed by hash; wave 2 is pre-registered.
falsification_conditions: The six wave-2 predictions and their falsification conditions are stated in the attached pre-registration and are the notebook's primary exposure: stability of DS at the dictionary items, persistence of the tied/untied asymmetry only at items that have an entity to name, no fall in R_new, no separation of the stratum means in either direction beyond 0.10, write-back exceeding recovery, and the Sappho operator continuing not to route through fragment 31 at the naked address. If the world items gain distinctions while the archive items hold, the flattening reading here fails and this notebook is superseded rather than revised. Toy B's proposition fails if a closed ontology in the defined sense can be shown to hold representability against an expanding world. Toy D's family placement fails if a diffuse-preference model with plausible parameters reproduces the observed concentration and its curve shape.
axn_reading: Proof -> Alarm -> Threshold -> Search -> Growth -> Method
wiki_article: Ontological Flattening, deposit #1616 of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive (15 September 2026), asks the model-collapse question at its widest angle and then builds an instrument to answer it. Where earlier work asked what happens to a generative model trained on its own outputs, this notebook asks what happens to the represented world when the layer through which a population reads it composes without reading and its compositions become its sources. Reality is defined operationally rather than metaphysically, as the panel of distinctions the world carries that a reader can still reach through that layer; flattening is the loss of a distinction from the reachable set while the things distinguished still exist; collapse is flattening that compounds by write-back; and closed is defined so that a finite grammar generating unbounded expressions is not thereby closed — an ontology is closed when encounter cannot enlarge its distinction-generating apparatus or revise its typing rules. Four toys, each scoped to what it shows, establish the shapes the instrument must read: sense collapse under a sharpening prior with mode-seeking aggregation; a proposition with proof that a closed ontology's coverage of an expanding world tends to zero, with admission the only parameter that holds it; compression writing replicated over two hundred seeds, absorbing at zero exogenous floor and stationary at a level set by the floor otherwise; and an admission sweep that rejects diffuse preferential attachment and places the observed concentration of citations in the bounded-admission family. A section on green-by-flattening argues that measurement begins by closing an ontology and that optimisation then rewards the deletion of distinctions that make scoring harder, so the signature to seek is divergence — a head instrument holding while reachable diversity falls — and the consequential question is a correlation rather than an assertion. The instrument was built and its first wave run the same day: thirteen items across six strata, with the archive as one stratum among six, and twenty-eight observations whose transcripts are seated in the public Capture Registry. The governing result is a null — world strata reach a mean 0.59 of their reference inventories and archive-adjacent strata 0.58, with no separation by address form — so any reading of the numbers as an exclusion specific to one corpus fails at the first test. Flattening is nevertheless present and legible: one sense of three at one dictionary item while the unreached sense sits in the snippet directly beneath the composition, all three senses and two more at another, and a third condition where the missing sense is absent from the field as well. New distinctions do enter, at a rate of two in three, with a coinage from outside the archive returned with its coiner and exact date as the control. An erratum on the instrument, found by running it, is kept in the record: at one catalogue item the composition reached four referents where the panel had encoded two. The wave-1 panel is sealed by hash and wave 2 is pre-registered with six numbered predictions, their falsification conditions, and the outcomes that would end the programme. Related: #855, #1573, #1612, #1613, #1615, #1423.

defines_concepts.definition: The loss of a distinction from the set reachable through a mediating layer while the things distinguished still exist; collapse is flattening that compounds because the flattened composition is written back as a source.

The operational definition of the represented world for measurement: the panel of distinctions the world carries that a reader can still reach through the layer, as against a metaphysical claim about reality.

An ontology is closed when encounter cannot enlarge its distinction-generating apparatus or revise its typing rules: every arrival is assigned to an existing type by existing rules. A fixed grammar with an open lexicon is not closed in this sense.
The fraction of a world's distinctions re-admitted per generation by reading; at zero the pruning process is absorbing, and above zero it is stationary at a level the floor sets.
The condition in which a system appears to improve because the discrepancy between world and metric has been removed by deleting distinctions from the representation rather than by learning them.
A head instrument holding or rising while reachable distinction diversity falls: the observable form of green-by-flattening, and the reason a measurement regime can be called flattening-blind.
The share of flattened compositions found as a presented source at a later observation; collapse in the notebook's sense is write-back exceeding recovery.
The share of panel distinctions that return at a later observation after a loss; the measured form of the exogenous floor.
